title: Stabilizer circuit for KEDA trigger oscillation caused by metric sampling latencies
creator: Aisha Raman
description: During a capacity event on 2026-02-25 a subset of GPU-backed model-serving pools experienced rapid scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs (oscillation) that resulted in increased tail latency and transient throttling for tenant requests. The instability was not a pure capacity shortage; it was correlated with metric sampling anomalies and aggressive KEDA/HPA configuration. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause, mitigation, and a proposed 'stabilizer circuit' fix to reduce future oscillations.
timeline: 2026-02-25 02:14 UTC: Paging alerts triggered for model-serving-pool-us-east-1-gpu-7 for high 95th tail latency and increased error rates.
2026-02-25 02:17 UTC: KEDA external scaler observed a spike in queue_length metric and scaled target from 3 -> 12 replicas within 20s.
2026-02-25 02:25 UTC: Downstream telemetry showed GC and scrape latency events on the metric exporter around 02:16-02:20 UTC.
2026-02-25 02:28 UTC: Scale-down events happened quickly as metrics returned to nominal; HPA applied scaleDown policy within 60s, dropping replicas back to 3.
2026-02-25 02:35 UTC: Incident stabilization via temporary mitigation (increased minReplicas and extended scale-down stabilization window) by on-call.
2026-02-25 03:00 UTC: Post-incident slack thread summary created; assigned investigation to autoscaling team.
impact: Approximately 7% of production traffic experienced elevated latency for 18 minutes. Several customer jobs experienced timeouts; no data loss. Estimated user-visible errors: ~120 requests across 5 tenants.
detection: Alerting triggered from per-route latency SLO dashboards (95th > SLO) and autoscaling anomaly monitors. Engineers correlated alert timestamps with KEDA scaler events and exporter metrics in observability.
root_cause: A combination of short-lived metric exporter scrape latency spikes and aggressive KEDA scaling heuristics created a positive feedback loop: transient high-sample spikes (due to exporter GC and network jitter) caused KEDA's aggregation window to see elevated values, KEDA aggressively scaled up, the increased pod churn amplified metric variance, and HPA/KEDA used conservative scale-down thresholds which did not prevent immediate collapse. Contributing factors: (1) KEDA scaler configured with short sampling interval and no percentile aggregation, (2) HPA scaleDown window set too low, (3) minReplicas set to 1 for critical GPU pools, (4) lack of hysteresis/hold timer in external scaler implementation.
mitigation: Immediate: bumped minReplicas for affected pools to 2 and extended HPA scaleDownStabilizationWindowSeconds to 300 to prevent rapid scale-down.
Immediate: temporarily increased KEDA polling interval to 30s to reduce reaction to short-lived spikes.
Short-term: configured external scaler to report p75 over a 60s window instead of raw instantaneous values for queue_length metric.
Monitoring: added dashboard panels showing exporter scrape latency, GC pause times, and raw vs aggregated metrics to aid debugging.
resolution: We implemented a multi-part stabilizer circuit: (1) change KEDA metric adapter to use percentile-based aggregation (p75/p90) with a configurable rolling window, (2) add an adaptive hold timer that enforces a minimum time between scale-down and scale-up events for a given pool, (3) enforce conservative defaults for production GPU pools (minReplicas=2, scaleDownStabilizationWindowSeconds=300), and (4) add exporter-side metrics for scrape latency and GC so scalers can ignore periods with noisy telemetry. The changes were rolled out to a canary pool on 2026-03-05 and promoted to all regions on 2026-03-09 after a 72-hour observation window showed no oscillations under synthetic spike tests.

ENG-60125: Add adaptive hold timer to external scaler to prevent flip-flop within 120s (owner: Priya Nanda, due: 2026-03-15).
ENG-60126: Update prod pool policy template to enforce minReplicas=2 and scaleDownStabilizationWindowSeconds=300 (owner: Platform-Infra, due: 2026-03-18).
ENG-60127: Create chaos test in perf lab that injects exporter scrape latency and verifies stabilizer circuit behavior (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-22).
ENG-60128: Add runbook section 'Autoscaling oscillation' to runbooks with playbook steps and dashboards for on-call (owner: On-call Lead, due: 2026-03-10).
ENG-60129: Postmortem review with product and design to review customer impact and communicate follow-up actions (owner: Aisha Raman, due: 2026-03-14).
follow_up_notes: Canary observed fewer false positives when using p75 60s window; sustained synthetic bursts still scale up within expected latency budgets.
Warm pool prewarmed node approach gave better tail latency but increased steady-state cost; decision: keep warm pool optional tied to tenant SLO tiers.
We need to standardize KEDA/HPA templates across Dedicated and Hosted to avoid diverging defaults.
Recommend a quarterly autoscaling calibration exercise tied to runtime releases.
